vectors.title: String has no maximum length
vectors.why: Without a maximum length, one request can carry megabytes into parsers, logs and the database.
vectors.applies: every string parameter or body field

vectors.title: String accepts any characters (no pattern, format or enum)
vectors.why: A string with no pattern, enum or strict format accepts any text, so injection payloads reach the handler.
vectors.applies: every string parameter or body field that is not an enum

vectors.title: Required string accepts the empty value
vectors.why: A required string with no minimum length, pattern, enum or format accepts "", which handlers often treat as a real value.
vectors.applies: required string parameters and required body properties

vectors.title: Header value is not constrained
vectors.why: A header parameter with no pattern, enum or format can carry line breaks, which is how header injection and response splitting start.

vectors.title: Pattern is not anchored with ^ and $
vectors.why: An unanchored pattern matches a substring, so a payload hidden inside an otherwise valid value passes.

vectors.title: Pattern accepts a known attack payload
vectors.why: The pattern is run against SQL, path-traversal, template and script payloads; any it accepts is a hole.

vectors.title: Pattern accepts an encoded form of a payload it blocks
vectors.why: A pattern that blocks a literal character can still accept its percent-encoded, double-encoded or overlong form.

vectors.title: Pattern can backtrack catastrophically
vectors.why: Nested quantifiers make a backtracking regex engine run for minutes on one crafted value.

vectors.title: Number has no minimum and maximum
vectors.why: A number with no minimum and maximum lets a caller send values that overflow, go negative or exhaust resources.

vectors.title: Integer has no int32 or int64 format
vectors.why: An integer with no int32 or int64 format leaves its width undefined, so large values overflow in typed languages.

vectors.title: Count, size or id accepts negative values
vectors.why: A count, size or offset that can be negative breaks length arithmetic and slicing.
vectors.applies: integer fields named like a count, size, limit or offset

vectors.title: Page size has no maximum
vectors.why: A page-size parameter with no maximum lets one call return the whole table.
vectors.applies: query parameters named limit, size, per_page and similar

vectors.title: Array has no maximum number of items
vectors.why: An array with no maximum item count lets one request carry millions of elements.

vectors.title: Array items have no type
vectors.why: An array whose items have no type accepts anything, including nested objects.

vectors.title: Array query parameter is unbounded (parameter pollution)
vectors.why: A query array with no maximum lets a caller repeat the parameter to pollute or exhaust it.

vectors.title: Request object accepts unknown properties (mass assignment)
vectors.why: A request body that allows extra properties can be bound to fields the client was never meant to set (mass assignment).
vectors.applies: every object in a request body

vectors.title: Request object declares no required properties
vectors.suggest: the properties a request must have
vectors.why: A request body object with no required fields accepts an empty or partial object.
vectors.applies: every object in a request body

vectors.title: Open map has no maximum property count
vectors.why: An open map in a request body with no maximum property count lets one request carry an unbounded number of keys.
vectors.applies: request body objects that allow additional properties

vectors.title: File upload has no size limit
vectors.why: An upload with no size limit can fill the disk or memory.
vectors.applies: fields that accept a file (binary strings)

vectors.title: File upload accepts any content type
vectors.why: An upload that accepts any content type can carry executables or scripts.
vectors.applies: fields that accept a file (binary strings)

vectors.title: Identifier is a sequential integer (enumerable)
vectors.why: A sequential integer id can be walked one by one to read other people's records.

vectors.title: Path parameter is not constrained
vectors.why: A string in the path with no pattern, enum or strict format can carry ../ and encoded slashes into file and route lookups.

vectors.title: Body accepts an encoding that has no schema
vectors.suggest: remove the content type or give it a schema
vectors.why: When a body is accepted in several encodings and only one has a schema, the others skip validation.
vectors.applies: operations whose request body offers more than one content type

vectors.title: Request body accepts a wildcard media type
vectors.why: A wildcard request media type (*/*) accepts any encoding, so a body can be parsed in a way the schema never described.
vectors.applies: operations that have a request body

vectors.title: Text body declares no charset
vectors.why: A text body with no charset can be decoded two ways, which is how encoding tricks bypass filters.

vectors.title: Operation does not declare its security
vectors.suggest: a security requirement, or security: [] if public on purpose
vectors.why: An operation with no security says nothing about who may call it; clients and gateways read it as open.

vectors.title: State-changing operation is not required to authenticate
vectors.why: A POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE that is public or optional lets anyone change state. Reads are graded separately.
vectors.applies: POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE operations

vectors.title: Operation accepts basic auth or an API key in the query
vectors.why: HTTP basic auth and API keys in the query string leak credentials into logs and referrers.

vectors.title: OAuth requirement names no scopes
vectors.why: An OAuth operation that names no scope grants access to any valid token.
vectors.applies: operations using OAuth 2 or OpenID Connect

vectors.title: Personal data travels in the URL
vectors.why: Personal data in a path or query string is written to access logs, proxies and browser history.
vectors.applies: operations where personal data was detected in a parameter or request body field

vectors.title: Operation declares no 4xx response
vectors.why: Without a documented 4xx, clients and tests have nothing to check rejected input against.

vectors.title: Error response has no schema
vectors.why: Without a schema for 4xx and default responses each service invents its own error body, which is where stack traces and internal ids leak.
vectors.applies: operations that declare a 4xx or default response

vectors.title: Operation declares no 429 response
vectors.why: A documented 429 tells clients rate limiting exists; without it the operation reads as unlimited.

vectors.title: Response object can carry unknown properties (data exposure)
vectors.why: A response object that allows extra properties can leak fields the schema never named.

vectors.title: Server is plain http
vectors.why: A server URL on http sends traffic, tokens and cookies in clear text.
vectors.applies: every server that names a scheme

vectors.title: Server variable accepts any value
vectors.why: A server variable with no enum lets a caller point the client at any host or port.
